rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.2 - two-season (postharvest 2017, fruit growth 2018) field experiment in a 0.5 ha nectarine orchard with a control (100% ETc, Allen et al. approach) and a PDI treatment triggered automatically by capacitance-probe soil water content thresholds via telemetry and electro-hydraulic valves, four replicates. Q2: Section 3.1 and Figure 2B - seasonal irrigation measured by in-line water meters was 420.4 mm (control) vs 251.6 mm (PDI), a mean reduction of about 40%; Conclusions restate that SWC-based PDI used 40% less irrigation than the traditionally scheduled treatment. Q4: Section 2.2, Figures 1 and 2C, Section 3.2 - soil water content in the 0-0.5 m profile and relative extractable water were monitored continuously; PDI reduced REW by up to 15% in postharvest and 4% in fruit growth while control stayed near field capacity, and Figure 3A shows the resulting plant water status (stem water potential ~0.25 MPa lower in PDI).
rows.notes: Water saving measured only by water meters (one method, Q3 no). Single orchard, single cultivar, single clay-loam soil in Murcia (Q5, Q6 no). Conclusion scopes the strategy to clay-loam soils in Mediterranean areas but does not state this as a requirement from its own findings (Q7 no). No limitation of the water-saving result is stated; limitations discussed concern the remote-sensing indexes (Q8 no). Irrigation totals given without SD/SE or range (Q9 no).

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.2 and 2.5 - field experiment with control vs sensor-based PDI treatments, yield measured on 16 trees per treatment at harvest 30 April 2018. Q2: Section 3.3 and Table 1 - no significant differences between control and PDI for yield, number of fruits, fruit mass, crop load or crop WUE (yield 8.37 vs 6.24 t/ha, ns); Conclusions state PDI used 40% less water with no yield penalty. Q4: Sections 2.2, 3.2, Figures 1-3 - soil water content/REW in the root zone and plant water status (stem water potential, gas exchange) were measured as the intermediate variables linking the SWC-triggered irrigation to tree performance (PDI <U+03A8>stem minimum -1.7 MPa, below reported damage thresholds). Q9: Table 1 - yield and yield components reported as means <U+00B1> SE (n = 4 replicates).
rows.notes: Yield in PDI was numerically ~25% lower (8.37 vs 6.24 t/ha) but not significant with n = 4; the authors note PDI did not raise crop WUE because of fewer commercial-size fruits linked to higher cracking after rainfall, and that yields were lower than in other reports due to management differences - these are caveats on interpretation rather than stated limitations of the result (Q8 no). Yield assessed by a single method (Q3 no); single site/crop/soil (Q5, Q6 no); no requirement stated for the effect (Q7 no).

notes: Full text available, including tables and figure captions; figures partly garbled by extraction but legible. The study's main aim is comparing terrestrial and remote water-status indicators; the water-saving/yield comparison between sensor-based PDI and ETc-scheduled control is a secondary result reported from one growing season (postharvest 2017 + fruit growth 2018).
